title: The Ford/Hill Project by Elizabeth Marvel and Lee Sunday Evans #thefo...
transcript: Well, this was an absolutely infuriating way to start the new year, but important nevertheless. The Ford/Hill Project is a verbatim documentary piece using transcripts from court hearings in which Anita Hill and Christine Blasey Ford bravely testified their experiences with two of our now Supreme Court justices. The four actors fluidly move between different people of different genders, adding a noticeable gender politics layer to the piece. I also think it serves to probe the audience to consider their own biases and how these kinds of accounts sit differently depending on the people delivering them. These two stories are smartly interwoven and unflinchingly direct, though they do carry a spontaneity by virtue of being verbatim text. I'm also making the assumption here that the actors are delivering their lines completely synchronously with the actual court audio bytes, judging by the earpieces they wear for pretty much the entire show. We therefore get a remarkably detailed delivery with the cadences and irregularities of unscripted speech. It's not just an impressive emotional feat for the actors, but a technical one too. The Ford/Hill Project is running through this weekend at La Mama. With that, another program for my collection.
